narrative_purpose: The cover that captures the chapter at a glance: an alien predator that reads instantly as a great cat, so the reader feels the uncanny familiarity the chapter is about before reading a word.
subject: A single large six-limbed predator standing in profile on a low rise, unmistakably cat-like in its lean muscular build and low predatory stance, but clearly alien: six powerful limbs instead of four, a flared armoured sensory crest sweeping back from the skull, and four forward-set eyes arranged in two stacked pairs. Faint bioluminescent markings trace its flanks. It is the clear focal subject, sharply lit against a softer forest behind.
scene: A dim bioluminescent forest clearing at night, glowing flora receding into haze behind the animal, a few drifting spores in the air.
camera: Naturalist three-quarter side view at the animal's eye level, the creature filling the central third of the frame.
light: The brightest light comes from glowing plants behind and below, rim-lighting the predator's contour in cyan; its own flank markings glow faintly.
palette: Cool teal-indigo dominant, the predator's body in deep shadow with cyan rim light, a single scarce warm magenta glint in its eyes to draw the gaze.
style: Hand-painted naturalist field plate of a real alien animal, textured and observed, not a film still.
detail_level: High on the animal's silhouette and head; soft and hazy on the background.
composition: Strong single focal subject with deep hazy depth behind, generous dark negative space above for the eye to rest.
consistency_notes: This predator is the thanator archetype and must read the same as fig-01 and fig-02. Establishes the chapter's creature look.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no UI chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
